description: Core permissions the shell needs to boot the app: its own window, the local server, dialogs for file picking, logging — and `default`, the app's own permission set (every command in `src/commands.rs`), which is what the shell's first-run/diagnostics page (`dist/index.html`) calls. Declaring the app manifest in `build.rs` switched the ACL on for local origins too, so this replaced their former implicit access. The store plugin is deliberately **not** granted: `tauri-plugin-store` does no scope check of its own (`store|load` takes any path, absolute or not), and the store it keeps (`preferences.json`) holds the unredacted database connection string. The shell reaches the store through Rust (`state::set_pref`), which the ACL does not gate, so the permission would expose the password and buy nothing.
